transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-06 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (CTO, Anthem), Mike Rivera (DevOps), Priya Singh (Security)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Samir from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account. we've got jordan our se with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Laura: good, thanks. excited to chat. we wanted to dig into private deployment options, networking mostly.
[00:20] Jordan: awesome. quick agenda — understand your current infra, CIDR/region constraints, how you prefer private connectivity (peering vs private endpoints), and any security requirements like KMS or audit logs. sound good?
[00:29] Mike: yep, that works. just to set context — we're AWS-first, multiple accounts per environment, strict egress rules, and some data must stay in us-east-1 due to residency.
[00:40] Priya: and security side — SOC2 is baseline, we also have customer data classification rules, key management via our KMS, and need audit trails.
[00:51] Jordan: great, yea that aligns with a lot of our private customers. quick question: are you leaning towards VPC peering or a PrivateLink-like setup? each has tradeoffs.
[01:02] Laura: honestly we were unclear — peering seems simpler but we've been told cross-region peering can be messy. PrivateLink sounds secure but we've got a lot of accounts.
[01:15] Samir: right — succinctly, peering gives you direct route-level access between VPCs but requires distinct peering sessions and route propagation; PrivateLink (AWS NLB + ENIs) gives an endpoint per account and avoids route table changes but means you need to manage endpoints and there's per-endpoint pricing.
[01:34] Jordan: also, with peering you can get lower latency but you have to watch overlapping CIDRs. we often recommend PrivateLink for high security multi-account orgs because it reduces blast radius and is easier for RBAC on the control plane.
[01:50] Mike: overlap is a problem for us, we have some legacy ranges that collide. can you support transitive routing via a transit gateway?
[02:02] Jordan: we don't depend on transitive peering, but Redwood Private can be fronted by a transit gateway — we've seen customers use TGW plus VPC attachments to centralize. note that TGW has its own routing constraints and costs.
[02:16] Priya: for KMS, we need Redwood to integrate with our customer-managed key so data at rest is encrypted to our KMS. is that supported?
[02:25] Samir: yes — we support CMKs. there's a small ops chore for key grants between your account and the Redwood service role in a private deployment; we'll share exact steps in the security pack.
[02:36] Laura: what about audit logs and retention — we need 1 year of immutable logs for access and usage.
[02:44] Jordan: we capture audit logs and can ship them to your S3 or SIEM. retention policy is configurable, but for immutable retention you'll want to set S3 object lock or a separate archival process. we'll include our logging integration doc.
[02:59] Mike: region question — some of our workloads must remain in us-east-1, but a few dev teams are in eu-west-1. can Redwood run in multiple regions and still present a single control plane?
[03:12] Samir: yes — Redwood's control plane can be regionalized; in Private deployments you can choose to host inference runtime in selected regions. important note: cross-region KV cache sharing is not something we recommend for low-latency workloads. usually you route requests to nearest region.
[03:30] Laura: so if we keep PII in us-east-1, we can still have analytics in eu-west-1? any data crossing concerns?
[03:39] Priya: we typically require that model context containing PII never leaves the region. how would that be enforced?
[03:45] Jordan: you'd enforce that at the routing layer — requests with PII tags go to us-east-1 endpoints only, and you can set SLO/fallback rules to failover to a degraded model variant with redaction. we'll show the config we use for per-route region pins.
[04:01] Mike: networking specifics — what ports and subnets do we need to open? can you give a minimal egress policy?
[04:10] Jordan: yes, minimal: allow egress from your subnets to our private endpoints on TLS 443; for peering you open the specific port ranges we list (usually 443 and a few ephemeral ranges for control plane). also, if using PrivateLink you create interface endpoints in each account/subnet. we'll share a CloudFormation example.
[04:30] Laura: any requirement for NAT gateways? we try to avoid NAT where possible for cost reasons.
[04:36] Samir: for private endpoints, NAT isn't required for traffic to Redwood. if you have scheduled model updates or external pulls then an outbound NAT might be used. we'll document options.
[04:49] Priya: certificate and TLS — do you terminate TLS at your load balancer? what about mTLS options?
[04:55] Jordan: TLS is terminated at the service edge; we support mTLS for customers who need mutual auth. that requires provisioning certs or using AWS Private CA. it's extra setup but we've done it with healthcare customers.
[05:09] Mike: how do you handle upgrades/rollouts — we don't want downtime when you patch the runtime.
[05:15] Jordan: Redwood Dedicated/Private supports canary and rolling rollouts; the control plane orchestrates canaries and there's automatic fallback. we'll include SLO/uptime SLA language in the enterprise docs.
[05:28] Laura: latency vs cost — what are typical examples for our expected workload? we have synchronous chat features at sub-300ms target.
[05:36] Samir: for sub-300ms you'd want colocated inference in us-east-1 with optimized batching disabled for latency-sensitive endpoints. cost increases with dedicated GPUs and lower batching, we can send a few reference benchmarks from similar healthcare customers.
[05:53] Mike: benchmark request — we'd like a lab run from our dataset, maybe a small POC. what's the timeline?
[06:00] Samir: typical POC is 2-4 weeks; first step is network connectivity + sample dataset + acceptance criteria. we'll propose a POC scoping doc after this call.
[06:12] Priya: compliance — do you have a SOC2 report we can review and an option for on-prem or air-gapped?
[06:19] Samir: we have SOC2 reports and we offer a Private on-prem package for air-gapped scenarios. SOC2 will be in the pack I email.
[06:29] Jordan: one more technical note on CIDR collisions: if you have overlapping ranges we usually recommend either readdressing or using PrivateLink per-account endpoints to avoid route conflicts.
[06:41] Mike: readdressing is painful; PrivateLink seems more realistic for our setup. what's the per-endpoint operational overhead?
[06:49] Jordan: you create ENIs in target subnets, and you pay per-GB and per-endpoint; operationally you manage endpoint security groups and policies. for a large number of accounts we can automate endpoint creation via CloudFormation or TF module we provide.
[07:08] Laura: are there known gotchas with AWS Transit Gateway and Redwood?
[07:13] Jordan: TGW works but keep in mind it introduces a single point of routing change and costs. also TGW doesn't support some cross-account flow logs the same way; we'll call that out in the doc.
[07:25] Samir: ok, let me recap real quick — items: we'll send network checklist + CF/Terraform examples, security pack (SOC2, KMS integration steps), sample cost ballpark, and propose POC scope. Jordan will prepare diagrams for peering vs PrivateLink and automation examples. Mike to share CIDR ranges and region constraints. does that match everyone's expectations?
[07:48] Mike: yep, that's perfect.
[07:51] Priya: yes, thanks.
[07:53] Laura: timeline — can we get the docs by end of next week?
[07:57] Samir: yes, i'll send initial docs by 2026-03-08, Jordan will aim for the diagrams by 2026-03-10.
[08:05] Jordan: quick question — are there any third-party appliances (like on-prem proxies) in-line we should know about?
[08:12] Mike: we have a Zscaler proxy for egress in some accounts; that may affect private connection tests.
[08:20] Jordan: noted, we'll include proxy testing tips.
[08:24] Priya: can you also include recommended IAM roles and least-privilege policies?
[08:29] Samir: yes — we'll attach IAM role templates and a checklist for least privilege.
[08:36] Laura: ok, can we schedule the deep technical session — how about Tue 2026-03-16 15:00 PST?
[08:43] Samir: works for us, i'll send a calendar invite.
[08:46] Mike: outstanding — thanks.
[08:48] Samir: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the pack and next steps. bye.

Notes: occasional minor transcription errors present; product name sometimes heard as "Redwood Infrence" in auto-transcript. References shared: networking checklist (link: https://redwood.ai/networking-guide), security pack placeholder (link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack).
